It would truly be a once-in-a-lifetime setting where intellect and imagination merged with camaraderie and warm laughter. The evening would conclude with the guests sharing life-altering ideas, new perspectives, and lasting memories from their time at the table. In short, it would be a culinary journey through the ages, sparked by the unique connections forged during that special night.

If you are feeling a strong instinct to immediately file papers or leave the house, it would be sensible to take a break of several days or weeks before making any formal moves. Emotional distance is easier with time so wait until you’re feeling relatively calm before moving ahead. Because once the papers are filed your husband cannot just up and leave as this will be considered desertion and you will get an automatic advantage in court if those proceedings ever happen. Remember that divorce is usually quick outside of international marriage situations, so it is smart to avoid mentioning anything in public until the actual process is over. All major decisions should be made jointly, but the divorce law technically allows one party to move forward on their own even if the other spouse refuses to sign anything, so if your husband ever walks out you will just receive the money he owes with no further involvement from him. If children are involved, a lawyer can guide you through the safest path. After separation the court will take into account each parent’s relationship with the kids and usually only order visitation if the other spouse really misses them—so focusing on being the fun parent right now will rarely change the outcome. A simple agreement to maintain joint custody is usually enough under law, but the law is rarely relevant in the most basic sense and most parents work things out on their own. Because divorce settlements are not final until you sign them, it is safe to delay sending them to your partner until you are fully sure about what you want, since negotiations can always continue until you reach a deal you like.
